title: Field-scalar stratified heart closure and locally closed support
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] such that its scalar ring $F=\Lambda(*)$ is a field. Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. On every scheme $T$ over $X$ use $R_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. An $R_T$-module is lisse if on a pro-etale cover it is a finite direct sum $R_T^r$, with $r=0$ allowed [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. A finite constant local model means a pro-etale local isomorphism $R_T\otimes_{\underline{\Lambda(*)}}\underline V$, with $V$ a finitely presented scalar $\Lambda(*)$-module and underlines denoting discrete constant sheaves. Constructible means having these models on a finite constructible locally closed scheme stratification [sk-def-sfb-constructible, def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-constructible-subset]. Assume that, on every locally closed subscheme $T\hookrightarrow X$, kernels and cokernels of maps between lisse $R_T$-modules are lisse and a short exact sequence with lisse ends has lisse middle term. Then the full class $\mathscr A_c$ of constructible $R_X$-modules contains zero, is closed under isomorphisms and under kernels and cokernels of maps between its objects, and is closed under extensions in the ambient module category. In addition, let $a:S\hookrightarrow X$ be a constructible locally closed immersion with a factorization $a=i\circ j$, where $j:S\hookrightarrow Z$ is open [def-weil-open-immersion] and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ is closed [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every lisse $R_S$-module $L$, the sheaf $G=i_*j_!L$ [def-sfb-module-lower-star, def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek] is constructible. More precisely its inverse-image restrictions to the three locally closed pieces $S$, $Z\setminus S$, and $X\setminus Z$ are respectively $L$, zero, and zero, with inverse-image coefficients identified with $R_T$; empty pieces may be omitted. Both extension functors here are exact, so their termwise application to $L[0]$ is $G[0]$ in the ordinary derived category [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories].

proof.text: Identify the scalar ring at the chosen terminal profinite set with that at PUnit using the section-ring sheaf on the unique terminal isomorphism. Reconstructing the ring from its internal multiplication and evaluating the monoidal sections functor give the same ring object. Transport a finitely presented internal scalar module to an ordinary module. Its finite free presentation makes its cokernel finite-dimensional, so Module.finBasis gives a finite basis. Reflect this basis isomorphism through the internal-module equivalence. The scalar-extension finite-free comparison in the existing local-model interface turns each model into a finite free module; conversely the point-pullback finite-free comparison gives a finite constant model for each lisse module, including rank zero.

For constructible modules A and B, choose their finite constructible scheme stratifications S and T. Use Stratification.inter: its domains are the actual fibre products of the old strata, and its immersion is the first projection followed by the old immersion. Pull back the old finite constant models along the two projections. The pullback-composition comparison and the fibre-product equation identify them with the restrictions of A and B to this single common stratification. No factorization is inferred from containment of subsets.

For a limiting kernel fork between constructible modules, use the common stratification of step 2. Exact pullback maps it to a limiting kernel fork on each stratum. Step 1 makes its two endpoints lisse; the assumed kernel closure makes its point lisse, and step 1 makes that point a finite constant model. This is constructibility of the original kernel point. Use the colimit-dual argument for cokernel coforks. For short exact sequences use common stratification for the two endpoints, exact pullback, and the assumed lisse extension closure; again step 1 supplies the middle model. The zero model and isomorphism transport are the existing proved generic constant-model helpers.

The closed immersion i makes Z locally Noetherian and topologically Noetherian. Its complementary open immersion and j are therefore quasi-compact. The condensed open-closed recollement gives exactness of i_* and an actual natural isomorphism i^*i_* ≅ id; j_! is exact by its definition. Apply the proved generic stratified_openExtension and stratified_closedPush helpers of the coefficient-heart extension module to the one-stratum lisse model. These helpers form open-closed stratifications with unchanged domains, transport models along the unit/counit, and use zero models on the complements. Thus i_*j_!L is constructible for this specified factorization, with no coefficient-family hypothesis.

For restriction to S compose the pullback-composition isomorphism, j^* applied to the closed counit isomorphism, and the inverse of the open unit. For any given closed complementary k in Z use the same closed comparison, followed by open_module_restriction_identities, to get zero. For every given complementary open v in X use the proved generic openRestrictionPushforwardZero helper: sections of direct image on an object over v are sections on its empty fibre product with Z, hence zero, and forgetting the module action reflects zero.

The degree-zero comparison needs only preservation of zero morphisms. Apply HomologicalComplex.singleMapHomologicalComplex first for j_!, then for i_*, and map both isomorphisms through DerivedCategory.Q. The resulting target is definitionally the degree-zero derived object of i_*j_!L. Exactness has already been established separately.
